key_insight: Optimal transport can be used to semi‑supervise lightweight alignment layers on frozen vision and language encoders to achieve strong cross‑modal alignment with far fewer paired samples than conventional contrastive approaches.
problem_solved: Reducing the large paired-data requirement for aligning pretrained unimodal vision and language models so that meaningful multimodal alignment is achievable with limited supervision.
method: Freeze pretrained unimodal encoders (vision and language) and add small alignment layers mapping each modality into a shared space.
Use an optimal-transport based objective to compute soft correspondences between image and text embeddings, enabling robust matching from few labeled pairs.
Train in a semi‑supervised regime that blends a small set of paired samples with abundant unpaired data via OT regularization and marginal/distribution alignment losses.
impact: Enables practical multimodal alignment when paired data is scarce, lowering annotation cost and making it easier to assemble cross-modal systems from existing unimodal models.
